doc.title: Jack Palmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 24, 1997

title: War years working in a defense plant in Rome
summary: He returned from California to work in a defense plant and play locally; few trumpeters were around.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: So what happened during the war years for you?

During the war years, well I came home from California, I came back to Rome during the war years. And where’d I work Jackie, do you remember? I had to go in a defense plant. So I says if I’m going to work in a defense plant, I might as well go home instead of in California, see? So I came back to Rome and I went to work in a defense plant. That was it. And played around town here.
Was there a lot of musicians in Rome that had to go in the service?
So it wasn’t hard for you to find work?

Well it didn’t matter anyway because there weren’t that many trumpet players around, there was only a couple: Tony Degrazio, and he was working burlesque in Utica; and Red Magno. There was only a couple of trumpet players, there wasn’t much competition let me put it that way. They were good though, these boys.
